results.content:
A Harvard CAPS/Harris poll conducted on September 26 found that 42 percent of voters had not yet firmly settled on their midterm choice.

That figure, Reeher says, is striking.

He said it would largely be expected that voters’ preferences would be more settled by this point, given that midterm elections generally serve as a referendum on the president, as well as considering Trump’s extensive policy agenda and low approval rating.
